q: All samples of matter can be divided into two categories: pure substances and ____.
e: Matter is broadly classified into pure substances (elements and compounds) and mixtures.

q: A pure substance is a form of matter that always has a definite and constant ____.
e: Pure substances have a fixed chemical composition and distinct properties.

q: Pure substances are classified as either elements or ____.
e: Elements consist of one type of atom, while compounds consist of two or more types of atoms chemically bonded.

q: At the beginning of the 19th century, John Dalton proposed the theory of matter: that all matter was composed of atoms, which were invisible and ____.
e: Dalton's original atomic theory stated that atoms were the smallest, indivisible units of matter.

q: Today, the atom is still considered as the basic unit of any ____.
e: The atom is the smallest unit of an element that retains the chemical properties of that element.

q: Elements are substances consisting of one type of atom, e.g., carbon element is made up of carbon ____.
e: An element is defined by having only one specific type of atom.

q: Atoms are the smallest particles into which an element can be ____.
e: Chemical division of an element stops at the atomic level.

q: There are 92 known elements which occur naturally, either in the free or combined ____.
e: Naturally occurring elements can be found uncombined (free) or chemically bonded (combined).

q: Substances like these, which cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means, are called ____.
e: Elements are the fundamental building blocks of matter and cannot be decomposed by ordinary chemical reactions.

q: On the basis of their properties, elements may be classified into two groups, metals and ____.
e: Elements are broadly categorized as metals or non-metals based on their physical and chemical properties.

q: Metals show metallic ____.
e: Metallic luster is the characteristic shiny appearance of most metals.

q: Most of the metals are malleable and ____.
e: Malleability allows metals to be hammered into sheets, and ductility allows them to be drawn into wires.

q: Metals are good conductors of heat and ____.
e: The free movement of electrons in metals makes them excellent conductors of both heat and electricity.

q: Non-metals are usually ____.
e: Solid non-metals tend to be brittle and shatter when struck, unlike malleable metals.

q: Most of the non-metals are poor conductors of heat and ____.
e: Non-metals generally lack free electrons, making them insulators.

q: The atoms of some elements are joined together in small groups called ____.
e: Molecules are formed when two or more atoms bond together.

q: A molecule of a compound (molecular compound) consists of more than one kind of ____.
e: Compounds are formed by the chemical combination of different types of atoms.

q: The atoms of different elements in the molecule of a compound are combined in a definite ___.
e: The Law of Definite Proportions states that a chemical compound always contains its component elements in fixed ratio by mass.

q: Hydrogen molecule is formed by two atoms of hydrogen, so it is a ____ molecule.
e: Diatomic molecules consist of exactly two atoms, which can be of the same or different elements.

q: In ammonia, there are more than three atoms from two different elements: N and H, so it is a ____ molecule (binary compound).
e: Polyatomic molecules contain three or more atoms.

q: In ethanol, there are more than three atoms from three different elements, so it is a polyatomic molecule ( compound).
e: Ternary compounds are composed of three different elements.

q: Mixtures consist of two or more different substances that are mixed physically but not ____ combined.
e: In a mixture, substances retain their individual chemical properties because no chemical bonds are formed between them.

q: They do not have well defined specific properties and the substances are not in fixed ____.
e: Unlike compounds, the components of a mixture can be present in any proportion.

q: The mixtures may also be heterogeneous or ____.
e: Mixtures are classified based on the uniformity of their composition.

q: Therefore, the mixtures can be classified as two main categories: homogeneous and ____ mixtures.
e: Heterogeneous mixtures have visibly distinct parts, while homogeneous mixtures are uniform throughout.

q: Apart from alloys containing two metals, solid-solid mixtures are ____.
e: Most solid-solid mixtures, like sand and salt, are non-uniform and thus heterogeneous.

q: Filtration is a method for separating an insoluble solid from a ____.
e: Filtration uses a porous barrier to separate solid particles from a liquid.

q: Crystallisation is defined as a process by which a chemical is converted from a liquid solution into a solid ____ state.
e: Crystallization forms solid crystals as a solute precipitates out of a supersaturated solution.

q: Decantation is a process to separate ____.
e: Decantation involves pouring off a liquid to separate it from a settled solid or an immiscible liquid.

q: Magnetic separation is used to separate the components of a mixture when at least one of them is ____ in nature.
e: Magnetic separation exploits the magnetic properties of one component to pull it away from non-magnetic materials.

q: Simple distillation is a procedure by which two liquids with different boiling points can be ____.
e: Simple distillation separates liquids based on differences in their volatilities (boiling points).

q: Fractional distillation is a method for separation of a liquid mixture into fractions with different boiling points by means of distillation, typically using a ____ column.
e: A fractionating column provides multiple vaporization-condensation cycles, improving the separation of liquids with close boiling points.

q: Centrifugation is a technique used for the separation of particles from a solution according to their size, shape, density, viscosity of the medium and ____ speed.
e: Centrifugation uses rapid spinning (rotor speed) to generate centrifugal force, separating components by density.

q: Chromatography is a separation method of the mixed substances that depends on the speed at which they move through special media, or chemical ____.
e: Chromatography separates mixtures based on the differential partitioning between a mobile phase and a stationary phase.

q: Chromatography consists of a stationary phase (a solid) and a mobile phase (a liquid or a ____).
e: The mobile phase can be a liquid (as in paper chromatography) or a gas (as in gas chromatography).
